chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn al-Ahmasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man said to him, 'May God rectify you. We have a butcher neighbor, and he brings a Jew to him and slaughters for him, until the Jews buy from him.' He said, 'Do not eat his slaughtered meat, nor buy from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat from a butcher who sells to Jews?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) extends the prohibition of eating the meat to include purchasing from the butcher, highlighting the significance of *ittisal* (continuous association) and commercial reliance on non-Muslims in early Shia jurisprudence. This ruling reflects the historical context of distinguishing Muslim identity through dietary practices and avoiding economic entanglements that might imply ritual approval of the Jews' consumption. It underscores the principle that the source of the meat, even if slaughtered by a Muslim, is affected by the primary consumer's status and the nature of their transaction.
